record.nameMeaning: "Heavy claw", for its large thumb claw
record.oneLiner: A fish-eating spinosaur with a crocodile-like snout and huge claw.
record.description: Baryonyx was a spinosaurid theropod from the Early Cretaceous of England, 7.5–10 m long, with a long, low, narrow crocodile-like snout and a very large claw on each first finger. Its numerous conical teeth and gharial-like jaws suited a fish-eating (and partly predatory) diet.

notableFacts.text: Named for the very large claw on each hand.
Its long, narrow, crocodile-like snout suited catching fish.
One of the most complete theropod skeletons found in the UK.
